items.title: A taut map from a pre-adic ring with finitely generated ideal of definition to a complete ring is adic
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a taut continuous map from a pre-adic ring with a finitely generated ideal of definition to a complete ring makes the target adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition, and the map itself adic (statement lines 1556-1563). The proof fixes a finitely generated ideal of definition of the source, forms the closures of the images of its powers in the target, and uses completeness to write the target as the limit of the quotients by those closures (proof lines 1565-1568). It then compares this with the adic completion of the target with respect to that ideal: the algebra statement for completions with respect to a finitely generated ideal identifies the quotients of the completion with those of the target, so the canonical map from the completion is continuous with dense image, and it is taut because the tautness of the original map identifies the image ideals (proof lines 1568-1575). Since a continuous taut map with dense image is open and surjective, the topology on the target is the adic one, which gives the conclusion (proof lines 1575-1578). The claim is H2: the construction of the two completions, the comparison of their quotients, and the final openness argument are each displayed, and the hypotheses enter at specified points.
